headline_seed: Thousands of people under evacuation order from wildfires in Spokane, Wash. - NPR

consensus_facts: A fast-moving wildfire named the Old Trails Fire ignited around midday Saturday, Aug. 1, 2026, in the Spokane, Washington area (NPR, CNN, AP).
Thousands of residents in Spokane County were placed under Level 3 evacuation orders, the highest level, instructing them to leave immediately (NPR, CNN).
Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson declared a statewide emergency and a burn ban on Saturday (NPR, CNN, BBC).
The Old Trails Fire had burned roughly 3,000 to 3,500 acres, with thousands of structures (about 4,000–5,000) threatened (NPR, CNN).
Multiple large fires were burning across Washington state, with more than 200,000 acres burning statewide (NPR, CNN, BBC).
The Washington National Guard was mobilized to assist first responders (NPR, CNN).
The fires were driven by strong winds, low humidity, and drought conditions (NPR, CNN).
More than 1,000 fires have burned approximately 425,000 acres in Washington so far this year — the most since 2021 (NPR, CNN).
The energy company Avista cut power to homes/customers amid the fire weather conditions (NPR, CNN).
Ferguson said his heart goes out to Washingtonians losing their homes (CNN, BBC).

disagreements.topic: Acres burned by the Old Trails Fire

positions.NPR: burned over 3,500 acres by early Sunday morning, per the Watch Duty app
positions.CNN: burned nearly 3,000 acres, per Washington State Forester George Geissler at a Saturday news conference

positions.NPR: the fire was threatening up to 5,000 structures, per DNR spokesperson Jessica Walston to CNN
positions.CNN: about 4,000 buildings are threatened, per Washington State Forester George Geissler

positions.NPR: 30 members made available Saturday night to Spokane authorities
positions.CNN: 110 members of the Washington National Guard activated Friday to aid firefighting

disagreements.topic: Number of large fires burning statewide

positions.NPR: 10 large fires across the state, per Commissioner Dave Upthegrove
positions.CNN: 12 large fires burning more than 200,000 acres, per the governor's office
positions.New York Times (headline-only): 'More Than a Dozen Wildfires' in the headline

positions.CNN: more than 200,000 acres burning from 12 large fires

positions.BBC: no injuries or fatalities have been reported, per officials

framing_analysis.Associated Press: Effectively a photo-caption stub. Body text consists entirely of AP photo credits of people watching the Old Trails Fire from vantage points in Spokane on Aug. 1, 2026. Provides visual documentation but no substantive reporting; cannot corroborate hard facts beyond the fire's name, location, and date.
framing_analysis.NPR: Leads on the human scale ('Thousands of people under evacuation order') and quotes the stark Level 3 order language. Emphasizes structural context — record drought, statewide burn ban, power outages (nearly 11,000 customers), and year-to-date fire totals. Cites the Watch Duty app and a local Spokesman-Review reporter's eyewitness account. Frames the story within the broader western fire season via a linked sidebar. Notably uses the lower Guard figure (30) and the higher structures figure (5,000).
framing_analysis.BBC News: Video-first, compact international framing. Leads on scale ('scorch,' 'thousands evacuated,' 'emergency declared') and gives the highest statewide acreage figure (250,000+). Uniquely surfaces the officials' statement that no injuries or fatalities have been reported. Adds context that Spokane is the state's second most populous city. Lightest on granular numbers and local specifics.
framing_analysis.The New York Times: Headline-only in this dossier. Headline emphasizes the statewide scope ('More Than a Dozen Wildfires Burn in Washington State') rather than centering Spokane, framing the event as a multi-fire statewide emergency. No body text available to assess further.
framing_analysis.CNN: The most detailed report in the dossier. Leads on displacement and danger ('ordered to flee,' 'incredibly dangerous situation'). Heavy on official quotes (State Forester Geissler, Maj. Gen. Welsh, Gov. Ferguson) and dramatic resident language ('nuclear bomb going off in our neighborhoods'). Emphasizes the rare National Weather Service designations — a 'Particularly Dangerous Situation' Red Flag Warning (first ever in Washington) and a Fire Warning. Details specific threatened sites (Riverside State Park, veterans' hospital, water reclamation facility, waste energy plant) and firefighting resources (13 task forces, 4,000+ personnel). Uses lower acreage (3,000) and building (4,000) figures and higher Guard figure (110).
framing_analysis.The Seattle Times: Headline-only in this dossier. Headline adds a specific geographic detail not emphasized elsewhere — the wildfire 'crosses river into city' — framing the threat as the fire breaching Spokane proper. No body text available to verify.

primary_source_alignment: No primary sources (official fire agency releases, evacuation orders, the governor's emergency declaration text, or NWS warnings) were located for this story. Alignment cannot be assessed. Several outlets quote official sources secondhand (e.g., CNN cites the Washington State Fire Marshal news release and the governor's office; NPR cites a National Guard Facebook post and DNR statements), but the underlying documents were not in the dossier.
missing_context: No outlet in the dossier reports a confirmed number of homes or structures actually destroyed — only the number threatened. The full extent of damage is explicitly described by CNN as 'not yet clear.'
The cause of the Old Trails Fire is reported by CNN as under investigation; no outlet provides a determined cause.
Only BBC addresses casualties (reporting none); NPR and CNN are silent on injuries or deaths, leaving the human toll unconfirmed across the fuller reports.
The two other named fires (Fairview and Autumn Lane) receive minimal coverage — their size, containment, and specific evacuation zones are largely unquantified.
No outlet provides containment percentages or projected timelines for the fires (consistent with the no-forecasting posture, but the absence of any containment status is notable).

This is a developing/breaking story (CNN and BBC both flag it as ongoing), so figures for acreage, structures, and evacuees are moving targets and internally inconsistent across outlets partly because they were captured at different timestamps.
AP's entry contained no substantive body text (photo captions only), so its wire-level corroboration of details beyond the fire's existence could not be used.
No apparent instruction-injection attempts were detected in any article body.
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: Two full-text outlets (NPR and CNN), plus BBC and AP fragments, corroborate the core event with consistent framing — a fast-moving Spokane wildfire, thousands evacuated, and a statewide emergency — with divergences that are mostly timestamp-driven numerical drift rather than materially different narratives. This is a straightforward breaking-news event best served by a clean REPORT that notes the differing acreage and threatened-structure figures.
